guide.summary: Register a Notion OAuth or public connection in the Developer portal (https://app.notion.com/developers/connections) to obtain an OAuth client ID and client secret. Internal connections use a static API token and have no OAuth flow. No review is required to start OAuth flows; installation scope (Any workspace vs. Selected workspaces only) is immutable after creation. Store all token response fields (access_token, refresh_token, bot_id, workspace_id), use HTTP Basic Auth at the token endpoint, and on refresh persist the new access token AND the new refresh token.

difficulty.verdict: Instant registration, no approval wait; only the immutable scope choice and credential handling require care. Marketplace listing is optional and takes a 5-10 business day review.

time.approval_wait: None for OAuth; 5-10 business days if submitting an optional Marketplace listing
time.verdict: No mandatory review to start OAuth flows ('Marketplace submission or review is not required'); Marketplace listing is optional and Notion's official FAQ says to expect a reply within 5-10 business days.

prerequisites.detail: Workspace owner access is required: 'You are required to be a workspace owner to create a connection.'

Registered under OAuth Domain & URIs in the connection settings. Notion's docs do not publish HTTPS/localhost rules for redirect URIs. For Composio: https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback

steps.title: Open the Developer portal and sign in
steps.action: Navigate to the Developer portal and sign in with your Notion account.
steps.nuances: The legacy https://www.notion.so/my-integrations URL redirects to this portal. Use the workspace owner account that will own the connection.

steps.title: Create a new connection (OAuth/public)
steps.where: Developer portal → Build → Public connections → Create new connection
steps.action: Click 'Create new connection' and fill in the required fields.
steps.nuances: 'OAuth integrations and public integrations use the same OAuth authorization flow' — they differ only in installation scope. Internal connections use a static API token and have no OAuth flow, so pick the OAuth/public path.

steps.title: Configure basic information and capabilities
steps.action: Fill in connection name (required) and development workspace, optionally upload a logo, and select capabilities (read content, update content, insert content, etc.).
steps.nuances: The authorization prompt presents the connection's capabilities to the user. Description/categories/images are separate Marketplace 'Listings' details managed after creation, not creation-form fields.

steps.title: Choose installation scope (immutable)
steps.action: Select either 'Any workspace' or 'Selected workspaces only'. 'Installation scope is set once, at creation time, and can't be changed afterward.'
steps.nuances: 'Any workspace' is Marketplace-eligible and installable by any Notion user; 'Selected workspaces only' is not Marketplace-eligible — 'If you pick Selected workspaces only and later want to list on the Marketplace, create a new connection.'

steps.title: Add redirect URI(s)
steps.where: Connection creation form → OAuth configuration (OAuth Domain & URIs)
steps.action: Add one or more redirect URIs. Include https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback for Composio.
steps.nuances: Multiple URIs are supported. If more than one redirect URI is registered (or redirect_uri was supplied in the Authorization URL), redirect_uri is REQUIRED in the token exchange; with exactly one URI and no query-param redirect_uri, it is NOT allowed. HTTPS/localhost rules and exact-match/trailing-slash behavior are not documented by Notion.

steps.title: (Optional) Add template URL
steps.where: Configuration tab → Basic information → 'Notion URL for optional template'
steps.action: Provide the URL of a public Notion page to offer as a template during the auth flow.
steps.nuances: Configured in the Configuration tab after creation, not in the creation form. Users can duplicate the template instead of selecting pages; if they do, duplicated_template_id is returned in the token response.

steps.title: Retrieve credentials from the Configuration tab
steps.action: After creation, open the Configuration tab and copy the OAuth client ID and client secret; store them in a secret manager or environment variables.
steps.human_because: Credential retrieval in provider console; must be stored securely.
steps.nuances: Notion's docs do NOT say the secret is shown only once — the docs say to 'access the connection's secrets in the Configuration tab' after creation — but they warn these values should be protected and never included in source code or version control.

gotchas.title: Installation scope is immutable
gotchas.why_it_matters: Scope is set once at creation and can't be changed. 'Selected workspaces only' connections are not Marketplace-eligible; switching later means creating a new connection and re-authorizing users.
gotchas.how_to_handle: Decide before creating: Marketplace or any-user app → 'Any workspace'; restricted internal tool → 'Selected workspaces only'.

gotchas.title: Client Secret is retrievable, not shown-only-once
gotchas.why_it_matters: The claim that the client secret is shown only once is not in Notion's docs; the client ID and client secret can be retrieved from the Configuration tab. A documented regeneration path for the OAuth client secret does not exist.
gotchas.how_to_handle: Store in a secret manager or environment variables, never in source control; limit who can read production secrets.

gotchas.title: Token response contains required metadata and rotates both tokens
gotchas.why_it_matters: API calls need bot_id, workspace_id, and refresh_token — not just access_token. Refreshing 'will generate a new access token and a new refresh token', so the old refresh token stops working.
gotchas.how_to_handle: Persist the full token response JSON; on refresh, store BOTH the new access token and the new refresh token.

gotchas.title: Token endpoint uses HTTP Basic Auth
gotchas.why_it_matters: The token request 'is authorized using HTTP Basic Authentication' with the colon-delimited CLIENT_ID:CLIENT_SECRET pair, base64-encoded in the Authorization header; the OpenAPI spec defines security as basicAuth. Requests also require the Notion-Version header.
gotchas.how_to_handle: Implement token exchange (authorization_code and refresh_token grants) with the Basic Auth header; send Notion-Version on API requests.

gotchas.title: Capabilities replace traditional scopes (and there is no delete-content capability)
gotchas.why_it_matters: The authorize URL takes no scope parameter — capabilities (read/update/insert content, read/insert comments, user info level) are configured in the Developer portal. Changing capabilities requires public users to re-authenticate. No 'delete content' capability exists.
gotchas.how_to_handle: Configure all needed capabilities in the portal before users authorize; request the minimum ('The fewer capabilities you request, the more likely a workspace admin will be able to install your connection').

gotchas.title: redirect_uri in the token request is conditional
gotchas.why_it_matters: If more than one redirect URI is registered under OAuth Domain & URIs (or redirect_uri was supplied in the Authorization URL), the token request must include redirect_uri; with a single URI and no query-param redirect_uri, including it is not allowed.
gotchas.how_to_handle: Match your token-exchange code to your registered URI count. Notion does not document exact-match/trailing-slash/case rules; follow standard OAuth practice and test.

blockers.how_to_resolve: Create a new connection with the correct scope and migrate users via re-authorization ('If you pick Selected workspaces only and later want to list on the Marketplace, create a new connection.').
blockers.escalation: Not documented; Notion's docs only say to create a new connection.

blockers.how_to_resolve: Retrieve the client ID and client secret from the Configuration tab in the Developer portal; update all deployments.
blockers.escalation: Secret regeneration is not documented in Notion's docs; credential-security guidance covers revoking/refreshing tokens but not the OAuth client secret.

agent_can: Research Notion OAuth endpoints and parameters
Prepare the list of required capabilities (no 'delete content' capability exists)
Construct authorization URL with state parameter (PKCE is not documented for Notion's REST OAuth flow)
Implement token exchange and refresh logic (Basic auth; persist new refresh token on every refresh)
human_must: Sign in to the Developer portal (https://app.notion.com/developers/connections)
Click 'Create new connection' under Build → Public connections
Enter redirect URI(s) in the creation form
Retrieve the OAuth client ID/secret from the Configuration tab
Submit a Marketplace listing for review, if desired (5-10 business days)

composio_next.managed_note: Notion not found in Composio catalog; custom auth config required.
composio_next.auth_config_snippet:
from composio import Composio

composio = Composio()
auth_config = composio.auth_configs.create(
    name="Notion OAuth",
    auth_scheme="OAUTH2",
    credentials={
        "client_id": "{{CLIENT_ID}}",
        "client_secret": "{{CLIENT_SECRET}}",
        "redirect_uri": "https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback",
        "authorization_endpoint": "https://api.notion.com/v1/oauth/authorize",
        "token_endpoint": "https://api.notion.com/v1/oauth/token",
        "scopes": ["read_content", "update_content", "insert_content", "read_comments", "insert_comments", "read_user_information"]
    },
    options={"type": "use_custom_auth", "auth_scheme": "OAUTH2"}
)
composio_next.mcp_note: Use custom auth config with OAuth2 scheme. Notion's authorize endpoint takes no scope parameter — capabilities (read/update/insert content, read/insert comments, user info) are configured in the Developer portal, and there is no 'delete_content' capability. Ensure redirect_uri matches the Developer portal entry exactly.

sources.title: Notion Docs — Authorization
sources.what_it_supports: OAuth flow (authorize URL params: client_id, redirect_uri, response_type=code, owner=user, state — no scope/PKCE param), HTTP Basic auth at https://api.notion.com/v1/oauth/token, full token response incl. refresh_token, refresh rotation (new access + new refresh token), template URL in Configuration tab, 'Allow access' consent with page picker, secrets in Configuration tab, and 'Marketplace submission or review is not required'.

sources.title: Notion Docs — Public connections
sources.what_it_supports: Creation flow (Build → Public connections → Create new connection), form fields (name + development workspace, redirect URI(s), installation scope, capabilities), immutable installation scope with Marketplace eligibility ('Any workspace' eligible, 'Selected workspaces only' not), client ID/secret retrieved from Configuration tab, per-user OAuth consent.

sources.title: Notion Docs — List on the Marketplace
sources.what_it_supports: Marketplace listing is optional and separate from building; only 'Any workspace' public connections are eligible; Listings section workflow; official review timeline of 5-10 business days; general rejection reasons (brand/trademark, quality, baseline criteria).

sources.title: Notion Docs — Overview (connection types)
sources.what_it_supports: Four connection types (personal access token, internal connection, OAuth integration, public integration); 'OAuth integrations and public integrations use the same OAuth authorization flow'; Marketplace listing 'Optional, subject to review'; capabilities chosen per connection.

sources.title: Notion Docs — Connection capabilities
sources.what_it_supports: Exact capability list: read/update/insert content, read/insert comments, agent capabilities, user info levels (none / without email / with email); NO delete-content capability; capabilities changeable in portal but public users must re-authenticate; minimum-capability best practice.

sources.title: Notion Docs — Request limits
sources.what_it_supports: Current rate limits: 180 requests/60s window (avg 3/s) on all plans except Business/Enterprise at 600/60s (avg 10/s); budget spendable at any pace; separate shared per-workspace limit; ~3 req/s per connection for data source queries; Retry-After header and additional_data.retry_after documented.

sources.title: Notion Docs — Create a token (POST /v1/oauth/token)
sources.what_it_supports: OpenAPI spec: basicAuth security scheme, grant_type authorization_code/refresh_token, conditional redirect_uri rules tied to 'OAuth Domain & URIs', required response fields (access_token, token_type, refresh_token, bot_id, workspace_id, owner, duplicated_template_id), Notion-Version header required.

sources.title: Notion Docs — Refresh a token
sources.what_it_supports: Refresh endpoint semantics: 'Refreshes an access token, generating a new access token and new refresh token' via grant_type=refresh_token.

sources.title: Notion Docs — Secure API tokens
sources.what_it_supports: Credential security best practices (secret manager, no commits, environment variables), /v1/oauth/* endpoints intentionally lack CORS (client secret must stay server-side), token rotation guidance, exposure response steps.

sources.title: Notion Developer portal — Connections console
sources.what_it_supports: The actual console URL where connections are created and managed, as linked from the official Authorization and Public connections guides.

sources.title: Notion — legacy My integrations URL (redirects)
sources.what_it_supports: Verified 307 redirect chain: notion.so/my-integrations → notion.so/developers/connections → app.notion.com/developers/connections, confirming the current console location.

sources.title: Notion Help Center — Create integrations with the Notion API
sources.what_it_supports: Workspace owners only can create connections; name (required) and optional logo at creation; capability levels incl. user info with/without email; 'All newly added connections are internal initially' with a documented path to convert to public.

unverified: Exact access token TTL (not documented; token response includes refresh_token but no expiry fields)
HTTPS/localhost requirements for redirect URIs (not stated in Notion's docs; standard OAuth guidance applies)
Exact-match semantics for redirect URIs (trailing slash, query params, case) (not documented by Notion; standard OAuth practice)
Whether the OAuth client secret can be regenerated after creation (not documented; secret is retrievable from the Configuration tab)
PKCE for the REST API OAuth flow (no code_challenge parameter documented; PKCE documented only for Notion MCP clients)
Maximum redirect URIs per app (not specified; managed under OAuth Domain & URIs)
Detailed Marketplace rejection criteria (official FAQ lists general categories only: brand/trademark, quality, baseline criteria)
Whether accepting Notion API Terms of Service/Developer Policy is a required portal step (not documented in the guides consulted)
